search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting dengue cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for Florida during June 2025 (2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30), covering all target fields: confirmed/probable/suspected/unspecified cases, deaths, hospitalizations, dates, and subnational/locality breakdowns.
search_reasoning: Florida dengue surveillance is primarily reported through the Florida Department of Health (FDOH), which publishes arboviral/mosquito-borne disease surveillance reports and weekly/monthly epidemiological summaries. The CDC ArboNET system also aggregates state-reported arboviral disease data including dengue for the US. For June 2025, the most actionable sources are: (1) FDOH official surveillance pages and disease reports (highest authority for Florida-specific case counts, locality, and date data); (2) CDC dengue surveillance and ArboNET (national aggregator with state-level breakdowns); (3) PAHO/WHO situation reports (international validation, may reference US/Florida data); (4) news and media reports (may surface outbreak alerts or case counts citing official sources). The upstream planned queries use overly rigid date-range strings (e.g., "2025-06-01-2025-06-30") that are unlikely to match real document text. This iteration refines queries to use natural language time references ("June 2025"), agency-specific terminology ("arboviral," "mosquito-borne"), and targeted agency/program names (FDOH, ArboNET, CDC) to maximize retrieval of relevant official documents. The 4-query cap per iteration requires prioritizing: (1) FDOH official surveillance (highest yield, most authoritative), (2) CDC ArboNET/dengue surveillance (national aggregator), (3) PAHO/WHO situation report (international validation), (4) news search (supplementary, may surface case counts or outbreak alerts). Literature queries are deprioritized for iteration 1 as peer-reviewed publications for June 2025 are unlikely to exist yet given publication lag.

query_batch.query: Florida Department of Health dengue arboviral surveillance report June 2025
query_batch.query_rationale: FDOH is the primary authoritative source for Florida dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and locality data. Targeting FDOH surveillance reports with natural-language time reference 'June 2025' and disease-specific term 'arboviral' (FDOH uses this umbrella term for dengue reporting) maximizes retrieval of the most relevant official documents. This replaces the upstream q_exec_001/q_exec_002 which used an unnatural date-range string unlikely to match document text.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDOH Arboviral Disease Surveillance report, weekly/monthly epidemiological summary, or disease activity report for June 2025 listing dengue case counts by county or statewide.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Florida Department of Health (.fdoh.gov or .myflorida.com domain), official surveillance program authorship, tabular case count data with date ranges.

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET dengue cases Florida 2025 surveillance data
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system that aggregates state-reported dengue data including Florida. CDC also publishes dengue case counts by state. This query targets CDC's dengue surveillance pages and ArboNET data tables, which may include June 2025 Florida case counts, confirmed/probable breakdowns, and deaths. Complements FDOH data and provides cross-validation.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC dengue surveillance summary, ArboNET data table, or CDC dengue statistics page showing Florida case counts for 2025 (ideally broken down by month or including June).
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: CDC.gov domain, ArboNET program attribution, tabular state-level case count data.

query_batch.query: PAHO WHO dengue situation report United States Florida June 2025
query_batch.query_rationale: PAHO publishes regional dengue situation reports that include US case data, sometimes with state-level breakdowns. These serve as independent validation of FDOH/CDC figures and may contain evidence quotes, case definitions, and hospitalization/death data. Refines upstream q_exec_003/q_exec_004 by using natural language time reference and explicit PAHO/WHO agency names.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO epidemiological alert or dengue situation report for the Americas covering June 2025, referencing US or Florida dengue case counts.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: PAHO.org or WHO.int domain, official situation report format, epidemiological week references.

query_batch.query: dengue cases Florida June 2025 health department report
query_batch.query_rationale: News and media reports may surface dengue case counts, outbreak alerts, or official statements from FDOH or local health departments for June 2025 that are not yet indexed as official documents. Useful for identifying specific localities, dates, and case counts cited from official sources, and for discovering links to primary official reports. Refines upstream q_exec_009 with natural language time reference and without unnatural date-range string.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News article, press release, or health alert from June 2025 reporting dengue cases in Florida, ideally citing FDOH or CDC figures with specific case counts, county-level data, or death/hospitalization information.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Bylined journalism citing official health agency sources, press releases from FDOH or county health departments, publication date within June 2025.

expected_evidence: FDOH arboviral/dengue surveillance report with statewide or county-level case counts for June 2025
CDC ArboNET or CDC dengue statistics page with Florida 2025 case data
PAHO situation report referencing US/Florida dengue cases for June 2025
News articles citing official case counts, deaths, or hospitalizations for Florida dengue in June 2025
Tabular data with confirmed/probable/suspected case breakdowns
Evidence quotes with specific numbers, dates, and locations
expected_source_characteristics: Official Florida state health agency authorship (FDOH)
Publication or report date within or immediately after June 2025
Quantitative case count data with geographic and temporal specificity
language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. Florida is a US state; all official reporting from FDOH, CDC, and PAHO for this jurisdiction is in English. No Spanish-language queries are needed for this iteration, as the target is US state-level official reporting. Spanish-language queries could be considered in a future iteration only if seeking travel-origin country reports, which is out of scope for this task.
trust_considerations: Prioritize FDOH and CDC as primary authoritative sources for Florida dengue data
PAHO/WHO reports provide independent international validation
News sources are supplementary; only accept case counts that cite official agency sources
Avoid sources that do not specify Florida as the location or that aggregate US data without state breakdown
Be alert to travel-associated vs. locally-acquired dengue distinctions, which FDOH typically reports separately
Verify that report dates or data periods overlap with June 2025 (2025-06-01 to 2025-06-30)
stop_condition_hypothesis: Stop after iteration 1 if queries return FDOH surveillance reports and CDC ArboNET data with quantified case counts, dates, and locality data for June 2025. Proceed to iteration 2 if official agency sources are absent, data is incomplete (e.g., missing deaths/hospitalizations/locality), or only news sources are found without official backing.
warnings: Upstream planned queries used unnatural date-range strings (e.g., '2025-06-01-2025-06-30') unlikely to match real document text — all iteration 1 queries use natural language time references instead
Peer-reviewed literature queries (upstream q_exec_005/q_exec_006) are deprioritized: publication lag makes June 2025 literature extremely unlikely to exist in iteration 1
Structured database queries (upstream q_exec_007/q_exec_008) are deferred to iteration 2 if official agency sources are insufficient
Florida dengue cases are predominantly travel-associated; locally-acquired cases are rarer and may be reported separately — both categories should be captured
FDOH may use 'arboviral disease' as the umbrella category rather than 'dengue' alone in report titles

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong authoritative signals from floridahealth.gov (7 results including weekly FDOH arbovirus PDFs for weeks 22, 24, 25), epi.ufl.edu (with a June 14, 2025 snapshot citing 85 travel-associated + 1 locally acquired case), and the FDOH surveillance index page. However, critical gaps remain: (1) The FDOH weekly reports retrieved cover weeks 22 (May 31–Jun 6), 24, and 25 — but week 23 (June 7–13) is listed on the FDOH index and not yet confirmed retrieved as a full candidate, and week 26 (June 22–28) is missing from the confirmed June-window PDFs. (2) The epi.ufl.edu snippet references a June 14 snapshot (week 23 data) but the underlying FDOH week 23 PDF is not confirmed retrieved. (3) Deaths and hospitalizations fields are not yet populated from any snippet — a targeted CDC dengue statistics or FDOH disease-specific page may surface these. (4) The FDOH surveillance index (rank 8) lists weeks 22 and 23 explicitly — week 23 PDF URL needs to be targeted directly. (5) CDC.gov returned 6 results but none of the snippets confirm Florida-specific June 2025 case counts with deaths/hospitalizations. A focused iteration 2 targeting the specific missing FDOH weekly PDFs (weeks 23 and 26), CDC dengue US statistics for 2025, and a targeted news/outbreak search for Florida dengue deaths/hospitalizations in June 2025 will close these gaps within the 4-query cap.
